headline: You're never really where your body is
universal_truth: The present moment is the only place where life actually happens
fun_facts: Research shows people spend 47% of their waking hours thinking about something other than what they're doing
Studies link mind-wandering to lower happiness levels, regardless of what activity people are engaged in
Athletes who practice present-moment awareness show 25% improvement in performance metrics
discussion_questions: When do you feel most fully present in your day?
What pulls your attention away from the current moment most often?
How might your relationships change if you were more present?

hook.script: Right now, where is your mind? Chances are, part of you is already thinking about what's next—or replaying something from before. Today we explore why presence is so hard and why it matters so much.

cliff.script: Here's the paradox: we spend half our lives somewhere other than where we are. And studies show this mental time-travel has a cost. What do you think it is?
cliff.prompt: What's the real cost of not being present?

options.response: That's true—but there's something even more fundamental at stake...
Exactly. Harvard research found that a wandering mind is an unhappy mind, regardless of what we're doing.

fact1.title: The Wandering Mind
fact1.script: Harvard researchers tracked thousands of people and found a startling pattern: we spend 47% of our waking hours not paying attention to what we're doing. Nearly half our lives, mentally elsewhere. That's not a bug—it's how our brains evolved to plan and remember.

fact2.title: The Happiness Connection
fact2.script: The same research revealed something profound: people are happiest when their minds are focused on what they're doing—even if it's something mundane. It's not the activity that creates happiness; it's the presence. A focused mind is a content mind.

fact3.title: Training Presence
fact3.script: The good news: presence is trainable. Athletes, surgeons, and performers cultivate it deliberately. Simple techniques—noticing your breath, feeling your feet on the ground, really listening—build the muscle of attention. Each moment of noticing is a rep.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You can't control what happened or what will happen. But you can show up fully for what is happening. Right now is the only moment you can actually live. Make it count by actually being in it.

outro.script: That's today's lesson on the power of presence. Tomorrow, we'll explore what makes you come alive. Until then, practice arriving where you already are.

growTrack.title: Presence Practice - Arrival Moments
growTrack.learning_objective: Build presence through intentional arrival rituals
growTrack.activity: Before your next meal, pause for 10 seconds. Notice three things you can see, two you can hear, and one you can feel. Then eat with full attention for the first three bites.
